title: Stock Market Update: Apple, Tech Stocks Provide Support in Rebound Effort
text:
Strong: Information Technology, Materials, Financials, Energy Weak: Real Estate, Consumer Discretionary, Utilities, Consumer Staples Moving the Market
Apple (AAPL) and the information technology sector provide strong support for the broader market
A Financial Times report suggesting China and the U.S. are trying to reach a trade truce ahead of the G20 meeting has helped the afternoon rally
Political uncertainty in Europe after resignation of Brexit Secretary Raab; Prime Minister May's leadership, Brexit plan under pressure Apple, Tech Stocks Provide Support in Rebound Effort 15-Nov-18 13:05 ET Dow -84.55 at 24995.95, Nasdaq +21.17 at 7157.77, S&P -2.59 at 2699.13
[BRIEFING.COM] The S&P 500 has bounced back to its flat line after a lower start to the session in what's been another volatile day of trading thus far. Resiliency from Apple (AAPL 189.65, +2.81, +1.5%) and the information technology sector (+1.1%) have provided strong support for a comeback effort.
Meanwhile, the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average is flat, the tech-sensitive Nasdaq Composite is up 0.7%, and the small-cap Russell 2000 is up 0.4%.
Other strong-performing sectors today are energy (+0.6%), materials (+0.4%), and financials (+0.4%).
The oil-sensitive energy group has risen in tandem with WTI crude today. WTI crude is up 0.7% to $56.64/bbl. The EIA's weekly crude oil inventory report showed that U.S. crude stockpiles rose by 10.3 million barrels last week, above forecasts of around 3.2 million barrels.
In the financial sector, JPMorgan Chase (JPM 108.73, +1.39) is up 1.3% following the release of Berkshire Hathaway 's (BRK.B 215,00, -1.03, -0.5%) third-quarter holdings, which showed that the company has initiated a position in JPM. Berkshire also increased its position in Bank of America (BAC 27.52, +0.32, +1.3%) and several other notable financial names.
Conversely, the consumer discretionary sector (-1.3%) has underperformed with Amazon (AMZN 1578.48, -20.53, -1.4%) and housing stocks weighing on the group. K B Home (KBH 17.20, -0.15) has lost 17.3% after it lowered its Q4 guidance and reported quarter-to-date orders to be down 14%. Negative investor sentiment has trickled to home improvement retailers Home Depot (HD 176.61, -3.24, -1.9%) and Lowe's (LOW 93.24, -1.70, -1.8%).
In earnings, Dow components Wal-Mart (WMT 99.80, -1.73, -1.7%) and Cisco Systems (CSCO 49.96, +1.64, +3.7%) reported reassuring results. Wal-Mart beat earnings estimates and raised its 2019 fiscal year guidance, but has rolled over following a positive start. Meanwhile, Cisco reported above-consensus top and bottom lines.
Elsewhere, U.S. Treasuries have extended their recent climb, pushing yields lower across the curve. The 2-yr yield is down two basis points to 2.92%, and the 10-yr yield is down three basis points to 3.09%. Also, the U.S. Dollar Index is up 0.3% to 97.11.
In Europe, Brexit secretary Dominic Raab has resigned, along with several other ministers, putting pressure on UK Prime Minister Theresa May's recently cabinet-approved Brexit deal and her leadership. The British pound is near session lows, down 1.6% to 1.2788.
Separately, press reports indicate Italian League economic adviser Borghi is making waves about Italy possibly leaving the eurozone if the Italian League wins a majority in the next election. The Euro Stoxx 600 lost 1.1% today.
Reviewing today's batch of economic data, which included Retail Sales for October, weekly Initial and Continuing Claims, Empire Manufacturing Survey for November, Import and Export Prices for October, Philadelphia Fed Index for November, and Business Inventories for September: Total retail sales increased 0.8% (Briefing.com consensus +0.5%) following a downwardly revised 0.1% decline (from +0.1%) in September. Excluding autos, retail sales jumped 0.7% (Briefing.com consensus +0.5%) following an unrevised 0.1% decline in September. The key takeaway from the report is that it reflects healthy consumer spending activity that will provide a positive input for Q4 GDP forecasts. Core retail sales, which exclude auto, gas station, building equipment and materials, and food services sales, jumped 0.3%. Initial claims for the week ending November 10 increased by 2,000 to 216,000 (Briefing.com consensus 214,000). Continuing claims for the week ending November 3 increased by 46,00 to 1.676 million. The key takeaway from the report is that the weekly increases did very little to alter trends in the four-week moving average for both series, which remain near historic lows and indicative of a tight labor market. Import prices increased 0.5% in October. Excluding fuel, they were up 0.2%. Export prices increased 0.4%. Excluding agricultural exports, they were up 0.5%. The key takeaway from the report is that nonfuel import prices remain tame, up just 0.7% year-over-year, versus 1.4% for the 12-months ending October 2017. The Empire Manufacturing Survey for November increased to 23.3 (Briefing.com consensus 20.0) from 21.1 in October, bolstered by an increase in the index for shipments, inventories, the number of employees, and prices paid. The key takeaway from the report, which uses 0.0 as the dividing line between expansion and contraction, is that manufacturing activity in the New York Fed region continues to run at a good pace. The Philadelphia Fed Index for November fell to 12.9 (Briefing.com consensus 20.5) from 22.2 in October, as most component indexes fell back from stronger levels. The key takeaway from the report is that manufacturing growth slowed in the Philadelphia Fed region in November, yet it still remains in an expansion mode with a reading above 0.0.
